# Wrapcheck

A simple Go linter to check that errors from external packages are wrapped
during return to help identify the error source during debugging.

## What is Wrapcheck?

Wrapcheck is a linter that checks whether errors from external packages are
wrapped when returned. This helps identify error sources during debugging by
adding context at package boundaries.

## Installation

Go >= v1.22.0
```bash
$ go install github.com/tomarrell/wrapcheck/v2/cmd/wrapcheck@v2
```

Wrapcheck is also available as part of the golangci-lint meta linter.

## Usage

To lint all the packages in a program:

```bash
$ wrapcheck ./...
```

## Configuration

You can configure wrapcheck by using a `.wrapcheck.yaml` file in either the
local directory, or in your home directory.

```yaml
# An array of strings which specify substrings of signatures to ignore. If this
# set, it will override the default set of ignored signatures.
ignoreSigs:
- .Errorf(
- errors.New(
- errors.Unwrap(
- errors.Join(
- .Wrap(
- .Wrapf(
- .WithMessage(
- .WithMessagef(
- .WithStack(

# An array of strings specifying additional substrings of signatures to ignore.
# Unlike ignoreSigs, this option extends the default set (or the set specified
# in ignoreSigs) without replacing it entirely.
extraIgnoreSigs:
- .CustomError(
- .SpecificWrap(

# An array of strings which specify regular expressions of signatures to ignore.
ignoreSigRegexps:
- \.New.*Error\(

# An array of glob patterns which, if any match the package of the function
# returning the error, will skip wrapcheck analysis for this error.
ignorePackageGlobs:
- encoding/*
- github.com/pkg/*

# ignoreInterfaceRegexps defines a list of regular expressions which, if matched
# to a underlying interface name, will ignore unwrapped errors returned from a
# function whose call is defined on the given interface.
ignoreInterfaceRegexps:
- ^(?i)c(?-i)ach(ing|e)

# ReportInternalErrors determines whether wrapcheck should report errors returned
# from inside the package.
reportInternalErrors: true
```

## Example

If you've ever been debugging your Go program and seen an error like this:

```log
time="2020-08-04T11:36:27+02:00" level=error error="sql: error no rows"
```

Then you know how painful it can be to hunt down the cause when you have
many methods that return errors from the same external package.

The problem is that multiple method calls into external packages (like `sql`)
can return the same error. Wrapcheck helps you enforce wrapping errors at
package boundaries to add context.

### Before (unwrapped errors)

```go
func (db *DB) getUserByID(userID string) (User, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = $1;`

    var u User
    if err := db.conn.Get(&u, sql, userID); err != nil {
        return User{}, err // wrapcheck error: error returned from external package is unwrapped
    }

    return u, nil
}

func (db *DB) getItemByID(itemID string) (Item, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM item WHERE id = $1;`

    var i Item
    if err := db.conn.Get(&i, sql, itemID); err != nil {
        return Item{}, err // wrapcheck error: error returned from external package is unwrapped
    }

    return i, nil
}
```

### After (wrapped errors)

```go
func (db *DB) getUserByID(userID string) (User, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = $1;`

    var u User
    if err := db.Conn.Get(&u, sql, userID); err != nil {
        return User{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get user by ID: %v", err) // No error!
    }

    return u, nil
}

func (db *DB) getItemByID(itemID string) (Item, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM item WHERE id = $1;`

    var i Item
    if err := db.Conn.Get(&i, sql, itemID); err != nil {
        return Item{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get item by ID: %v", err) // No error!
    }

    return i, nil
}
```

Now, your logs will be more descriptive:

```log
time="2020-08-04T11:36:27+02:00" level=error error="failed to get user by ID: sql: error no rows"
```

## Why Wrap Errors?

Errors in Go are simple values that contain only an error message. When you
call external libraries which may return errors, wrapping the error at the
call site adds additional information about where the error occurred. This
makes debugging much easier, especially when multiple calls to the same
library can return the same error.

As of Go 1.13, error wrapping using `fmt.Errorf(...)` is the recommended way
to compose errors in Go to add additional information.

	Name: "wrapcheck",
	Doc:  "Checks that errors returned from external packages are wrapped",
	Run:  run,

func run(pass *analysis.Pass) (any, error) {
	// Load config
	cfg := defaultConfig
	loadedCfg := loadConfig()
	if loadedCfg != nil {
		if loadedCfg.IgnoreSigs != nil {
			cfg.IgnoreSigs = loadedCfg.IgnoreSigs
		}
		if loadedCfg.ExtraIgnoreSigs != nil {
			cfg.ExtraIgnoreSigs = loadedCfg.ExtraIgnoreSigs
		}
		if loadedCfg.IgnoreSigRegexps != nil {
			cfg.IgnoreSigRegexps = loadedCfg.IgnoreSigRegexps
		}
		if loadedCfg.IgnorePackageGlobs != nil {
			cfg.IgnorePackageGlobs = loadedCfg.IgnorePackageGlobs
		}
		if loadedCfg.IgnoreInterfaceRegexps != nil {
			cfg.IgnoreInterfaceRegexps = loadedCfg.IgnoreInterfaceRegexps
		}
		cfg.ReportInternalErrors = loadedCfg.ReportInternalErrors
	}

	ignoreSigs := append(*cfg.IgnoreSigs, cfg.ExtraIgnoreSigs...)

	var sigRegexps []*regexp.Regexp
	for _, expr := range cfg.IgnoreSigRegexps {
		sigRegexps = append(sigRegexps, regexp.MustCompile(expr))
	}

	var ifaceRegexps []*regexp.Regexp
	for _, expr := range cfg.IgnoreInterfaceRegexps {
		ifaceRegexps = append(ifaceRegexps, regexp.MustCompile(expr))
	}

	errorType := types.Universe.Lookup("error").Type()

	for _, file := range pass.Files {
		ast.Inspect(file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
			ret, ok := n.(*ast.ReturnStmt)
			if !ok {
				return true
			}
			for _, expr := range ret.Results {
				typ := pass.TypesInfo.Types[expr].Type
				if typ == nil {
					continue
				}

				// Handle multiple returns
				if t, isTuple := typ.(*types.Tuple); isTuple {
					for i := 0; i < t.Len(); i++ {
						if types.Identical(t.At(i).Type(), errorType) {
							checkExpr(pass, expr, file, cfg, ignoreSigs, sigRegexps, ifaceRegexps)
							// Do not break here because a CallExpr can return multiple errors?
							// A call like `func() (error, error)` could return multiple errors.
							// However, since expr is the whole CallExpr, we just evaluate it once.
							break
						}
					}
				} else if types.Identical(typ, errorType) {
					checkExpr(pass, expr, file, cfg, ignoreSigs, sigRegexps, ifaceRegexps)
				}
			}
			return true
		})
	}
	return nil, nil
}

func checkExpr(pass *analysis.Pass, expr ast.Expr, file *ast.File, cfg Config, ignoreSigs []string, sigRegexps []*regexp.Regexp, ifaceRegexps []*regexp.Regexp) {
	obj := getErrorSource(pass, expr, file)
	if obj == nil {
		return
	}

	sig := obj.String()

	// Check against ignore list
	for _, ignore := range ignoreSigs {
		if strings.Contains(sig, ignore) {
			return
		}
	}
	for _, re := range sigRegexps {
		if re.MatchString(sig) {
			return
		}
	}

	var isInterface bool
	if fn, ok := obj.(*types.Func); ok {
		s := fn.Type().(*types.Signature)
		if s.Recv() != nil {
			if _, ok := s.Recv().Type().Underlying().(*types.Interface); ok {
				isInterface = true
				ifaceName := getInterfaceName(s.Recv().Type())
				for _, re := range ifaceRegexps {
					if re.MatchString(ifaceName) {
						return
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	if isInterface {
		pass.Reportf(expr.Pos(), "error returned from interface method should be wrapped: sig: %s", sig)
		return
	}

	pkg := obj.Pkg()
	if pkg == nil || pkg == pass.Pkg {
		if cfg.ReportInternalErrors {
			pass.Reportf(expr.Pos(), "package-internal error should be wrapped: sig: %s", sig)
		}
		return
	}

	// External
	for _, glob := range cfg.IgnorePackageGlobs {
		if matchGlob(glob, pkg.Path()) {
			return
		}
	}

	pass.Reportf(expr.Pos(), "error returned from external package is unwrapped: sig: %s", sig)
}

func matchGlob(glob, path string) bool {
	matched, _ := filepath.Match(glob, path)
	return matched
}

func getInterfaceName(t types.Type) string {
	if named, ok := t.(*types.Named); ok {
		return named.Obj().Name()
	}
	return t.String()
}
func getErrorSource(pass *analysis.Pass, expr ast.Expr, file *ast.File) types.Object {
	for {
		expr = ast.Unparen(expr)
		if call, ok := expr.(*ast.CallExpr); ok {
			if sel, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.SelectorExpr); ok {
				if selInfo := pass.TypesInfo.Selections[sel]; selInfo != nil {
					return selInfo.Obj()
				}
				if obj := pass.TypesInfo.Uses[sel.Sel]; obj != nil {
					return obj
				}
			}
			if id, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.Ident); ok {
				if obj := pass.TypesInfo.Uses[id]; obj != nil {
					return obj
				}
			}
			return nil
		}
		if id, ok := expr.(*ast.Ident); ok {
			obj := id.Obj
			if obj == nil {
				return nil
			}

			var bestExpr ast.Expr
			var maxPos token.Pos

			ast.Inspect(file, func(n ast.Node) bool {
				if n == nil || n.Pos() >= id.Pos() {
					return true
				}
				switch stmt := n.(type) {
				case *ast.AssignStmt:
					for i, lhs := range stmt.Lhs {
						if lid, ok := lhs.(*ast.Ident); ok && lid.Obj == obj {
							if stmt.Pos() > maxPos {
								maxPos = stmt.Pos()
								if len(stmt.Rhs) == 1 {
									bestExpr = stmt.Rhs[0]
								} else if len(stmt.Rhs) == len(stmt.Lhs) {
									bestExpr = stmt.Rhs[i]
								}
							}
						}
					}
				case *ast.ValueSpec:
					for i, name := range stmt.Names {
						if name.Obj == obj {
							if stmt.Pos() > maxPos {
								maxPos = stmt.Pos()
								if len(stmt.Values) == 1 {
									bestExpr = stmt.Values[0]
								} else if len(stmt.Values) == len(stmt.Names) {
									bestExpr = stmt.Values[i]
								}
							}
						}
					}
				}
				return true
			})
			if bestExpr != nil {
				expr = bestExpr
				continue
			}
			return nil
		}
		return nil
	}
}

func loadConfig() *Config {
	// Look for .wrapcheck.yaml in local or home directory
	for _, dir := range []string{".", os.Getenv("HOME")} {
		if dir == "" {
			continue
		}
		path := filepath.Join(dir, ".wrapcheck.yaml")
		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err == nil {

			if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &cfg); err == nil {
